summary: Gate 1 round 2 preparation review of 5183e2d07cfbc77fe68438ee5396d136b7e787c3. All three round-1 low findings are resolved and verified against the archived originals: README now correctly describes job.sh as the 30-minute pr299-pilot wrapper taking a pilot/campaign argument (harness/job.sh lines 10,12,29) and names screen.py/nic.py/test_nic.py as SDF-era (nic.py uses /sdf/data paths, screen.py/test_nic.py reference Weka); the report (lines 111-114) explains FINAL_REPORT.txt's original paths and their relocations, which archive-map.json confirms (reviews/campaign-r1/review.json -> reviews/campaign-r1.json; snapshot/campaign-job-61375111 -> campaign-job-61375111/; plots/ retains only the PNG and CSV, no PDF); README line 57 lists analysis/analyze_campaign.py with a description matching its code. Packaging is internally consistent: SHA256SUMS has 629 entries = 595 evidence files + 33 scripts + 1 report; archive-map.json has 624 mapped entries = 629 minus the five non-preserved files (README, report, verify_archive.py, test_verify_archive.py, archive-map.json itself), matching the helper's 624 byte-preserved count. The new test_archive_rejects_tampering was traced through verify_archive.verify for all five mutations (modified, missing, extra, symlink, mapped_hash); each reaches the asserted error message before any other check. No trailing whitespace in the newly authored files. All Markdown link targets in README and report exist in the tree. No new blocker found. C1 remains blocking/unfixed and Run77 deferred, both still stated in the report; this verdict covers evidence-publication preparation only, not PR approval. One new low nonblocking advisory (G2-PYCACHE-COVERAGE) recorded. Hash values and the unit-test results were not recomputed or run by this reviewer; they rest on the helper's supplied evidence.

package_files() includes every regular file under SCRIPTS via rglob('*'). test_verify_archive.py imports verify_archive; if the tests are run without -B (or PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE), a __pycache__/*.pyc appears under the scripts tree and both test_complete_archive and all five tampering subcases fail with 'Checksum coverage differs' instead of the asserted messages. README line 72-73 prescribes -B, so this is a documented operational fragility, not a defect in the archive content. Pre-existing from round 1 (verify_archive.py unchanged); not a regression.
findings.requested_change: Advisory only; no change required for this gate. Optionally, in a later packaging revision, exclude '__pycache__' directories in package_files() or add a one-line README note that stray bytecode caches cause a coverage failure.
